text: I don't know your whole story, of course, but leaving even for a good job without receiving citizenship because of a missed date is very reckless. Just because you've been approved for citizenship doesn't mean you can get it at any time later. A condition for receiving citizenship is your intention to reside in Israel, which you've demonstrated throughout the entire process for several years. I know of cases where people were denied citizenship and their Aleph 5 visas were extended for another year if they accidentally mentioned plans to work abroad in the future during the final interview. Misrad Hapnim really doesn't like this. And if you leave now for a long time without receiving citizenship, there's a chance your visa won't be extended, the process will be interrupted, and your case will be closed. And then you'll have to start from scratch. So I highly recommend reaching an agreement with your employer to postpone the start of your job. In Israel, write or go to your local Ministry of Interior office and request a new date for receiving citizenship. But don't mention that you're planning to leave again for a long time. After the ceremony, you'll feel free.
